messages:
rachel: Heads-up — saw the quickstart leak rate credits when you combine pagination, high concurrency, and frequent token rotations. Getting short 429 spikes that confuse new users.

omar: Can you share minimal steps? sounds similar to other reports but could be a different root cause.

rachel: Repro steps: start quickstart with --concurrency=16 --page-size=1 then run a token-rotator that swaps creds every 1500ms.

rachel: Example repro script:
```bash
# run quickstart
./quickstart --concurrency=16 --page-size=1 &
# rotate token in a loop
for i in {1..200}; do sleep 1.5; ./rotate-token.sh; done
```

vince: Logs show duplicate fetches after refresh and a sudden window refill from the client side:
```
2026-04-20T08:11:02Z WARN auth: refresh for acct=beta-team
2026-04-20T08:11:02Z INFO paginator: fetch page=12 attempt=2
2026-04-20T08:11:02Z INFO rate: client_window reset -> remaining=100
2026-04-20T08:11:03Z ERROR http: 429 rate_limit
```

tara: That client_window reset is the tell. Some SDKs reset the sliding window on refresh which causes an immediate burst; others preserve the remainder. Quickstarts defaulting to the reset behavior will look like the server is flaking.

omar: Which SDKs do this? Node vs Python vs Go parity notes?

vince: Node default currently resets on refresh (historical intent: avoid negative remaining). Py preserves remainder. Go preserves but had a bug where jitter wasn't applied to refresh.

rachel: Temporary quickstart fixes: lower concurrency to 6, set REFRESH_JITTER_MS=250, and enable CLIENT_SMOOTHING=true. That removed the confusing 429s in my local tests.

tara: Long term: we should pick a single default for all SDKs — preserve remainder on refresh — and expose an explicit opt-in to reset for latency-first microburst apps. Also add sampleapp flags that are safer for onboarding.

omar: Agreed. I'll open a ticket to update SDK parity docs and the quickstart defaults. Also add an integration test that simulates token rotation during pagination to catch regressions.

ci-bot: Created issue #4332: "quickstart onboarding: client window refresh parity -> 429 bursts" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/issues/4332)

vince: I'll draft the SDK change: add preserve_window_on_refresh boolean in client config (default=true) and wire in a small unit test across node/py/go.

rachel: Also please add a short blurb in the quickstart readme explaining these flags and why you might still want reset behavior. New users keep thinking the API is unstable.

tara: PR opened for quickstart defaults: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/834 (enable smoothing + refresh jitter)

omar: Nice. After PR lands let's update the onboarding guide and SDK parity page with an explicit example showing the difference: preserve vs reset.

rachel: Verified PR branch locally — 429 spikes gone for my reproducer. Thanks folks! :tada:
